key_insight: The classical Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm is proved to stabilize in linear time, specifically within 5(n-1) iterations, closing the gap to the known Ω(n) lower bound.
engineering_relevance: This sharp bound improves worst-case guarantees for graph isomorphism-related routines and informs the cost of higher-dimensional WL methods used in graph algorithms and learning.
method: Analyze refinement dynamics of 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman colorings.
Derive a new upper bound of 5(n-1) rounds for stabilization.
Extend the argument to k-dimensional WL, giving O(n^{k-1}/(k-2)! + n^{k-2}) for k≥3.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical and compares against prior bounds, improving the previous O(n log n) upper bound while matching the Ω(n) lower bound asymptotically.
watch_item: The guarantee is about iteration count in the worst case; actual runtime still depends on implementation details and the cost of each refinement round.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
